question: In order to meet its obligations under the UN Sustainable Development Goals, the Autonomous Region of the Azores has brought forward the date by which to achieve the target of protecting 30% of marine areas: to 2024 from 2030. Fishers and fishing industry organisations in the Azores have raised concerns about the lack of support for the sector, which is set to face further curbs on its activity.

More so than anyone else, fishers have an interest in restoring, enhancing and conserving marine biodiversity, but they say that bringing forward deadlines before the necessary framework is in place could jeopardise attainment of the goals. Besides, support to enable the fisheries sector to keep working is needed now, not later.

What support can be channelled towards the fisheries sector in this outermost region to compensate fishers for any constraints on their activity that may result from these protected areas being set up?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.5.2024) The European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund 2021-2027 (EMFAF) can support financial compensation to fishermen in the context of marine protected areas (MPAs) if it contributes directly to the objectives of the Fund.

A first possibility is compensation, under specific conditions, for the temporary cessation of fishing activities1 due to conservation measures, including those necessary for compliance with obligations under Union environmental legislation adopted pursuant to Article 11 of the Common Fisheries Policy2 (in case applicable in the MPA).

A second possibility is financial compensation for income foregone or additional costs stemming directly from the involvement of the fisher in the management of the MPA3. The local fisheries communities can also receive long-term funding4 and decide how it is spent through local partnerships, called Community-led local development (CLLD).

CLLD funding is delegated to local partnerships that bring together the private sector, local authorities and civil society organisations. These provisions of the EMFAF Regulation are implemented under shared management by the Member States. Thus, the national authorities define the types of actions that they wish to support within their national EMFAF programme.

The selection and implementation of projects also fall under the responsibility of the national authorities, which decide on the selection criteria and specific conditions for support in line with their national programmes, which must contain an action plan for each outermost region, and with the regulatory and policy framework.
For more information, please contact the Portuguese Managing Authority5 or the Azores regional coordinator6.
